chapter: In The Mood, Rendezvous and Capitol
title: Nat King Cole, the trio, and singing
summary: Fields toured with Nat Cole, who told him he too had once said he could not sing; Parker Berry doubted Cole could be a vocalist.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: No. Nat was still living then and I did quite a few tunes with Nat--

So we went to talking and he says I heard a lot, they just went nuts over the Beatles, when they bought that tape of them and everything and it looks like they forgot about everybody, because they just didn't do anything at all.
In that session, Junior was on it--

Nat King Cole; I didn't know that. No, I didn't do any; I toured with him. I remember one particular that I'll never forget but show you really a lot of way that reputation that the Jews have; they kind of know what they're doing though. Parker Berry knew Nat Cole from the time that I think he was with Les Hines, when Nat first went to Los Angeles with that very good band, that broke up. He decided then, that the band broke up, so they decided to have a little trio. Well, they came through all right with the trio and were going and we were in the Paradise Theatre in Detroit and I don't know whether it's that particular time for certain, but I was in there with Nat, I played several times with Nat; but I was in there and Nat and I got to talking and Nat says you have a nice band, Fields, how come you don't sing or nothing sometimes? I said I can't sing and he said, now don't say that. I said why do you

say that? He said, I used to say that. He said I had a big band once and he said, I said I couldn't sing. The band broke up, I went and got a job with a trio and just playing an instrument but when the guy came up and said we had to sing I went jiving around because the man said if I played there I had to sing some. So that's the way this trio started and I always said I couldn't sing. And believe it or not, they are fixing now, to put me out as a singer.

And so just like we were talking, I got to talking to Parker and told him that they were going to put Nat out as a singer and he said, I'll be damned, he got away with that trio stuff and he ain't strong enough to be no singer, and then he named somebody else in the trio (inaudible).
About another six months later, they had a recording out about Nat King and there was no turning back.
